proven.why: Ten reported approvals so one filing or a duplicated count cannot carry the top tier (every count in the file is even, cause undocumented), and 90 percent so a visible denial history keeps a company out; p is the chapter 11 worked-example value for Proven, not a calibrated probability.

likely.why: Four reported approvals is still at least two if the even counts are double-counted, and 70 percent tolerates some denials; p is the chapter 11 worked-example value for Likely.

thin.why: A matching title exists but the counts or rate fall below Likely; 0.3 is an ordinal placeholder chosen so the scorer files the row under Skip for any timeline factor, not a probability.
